candidate_orientation_domain.meaning: same canonical orientation reference within a context
distinct orientations jointly admissible under a declared context
orientations with a declared ordinal relation
orientations requiring incompatible assignments under the context
no complete comparison rule is available

candidate_rules: EQUAL requires canonical reference identity within the same context.
COMPATIBLE requires an explicit context rule admitting both orientations.
ORDERED requires an explicit ordinal or orientation ordering relation.
CONFLICT requires an explicit incompatible-constraint witness.
INCOMPARABLE is returned when no equality, compatibility, order, or conflict rule applies.

conflict_precedence.guard: Precedence does not convert an unresolved case into conflict without a witness.

preservation_rule.statement: A comparison preserves orientation only if its result retains every orientation distinction marked relevant by Context.

open_obligations: Define the source and target domains of orientations.
Define whether COMPATIBLE and ORDERED can co-occur.
Define conflict witnesses and their provenance requirements.
Prove or test completeness of CompareOrientation over the executable context domain.
Define how orientation comparison feeds Lawful and MTO_Candidates.
nonclaims: No orientation fixture establishes universal admissibility.
No comparison result authorizes deterministic MTO selection.
No canonical orientation domain is created.
